final.label: debug-switch-or-output-left-on

skill_entry.name: 14. A debug switch, a debug dump, a debug-only include or a trace promotion that ships on
skill_entry.trigger: In a file under h/ or src/ (never t/), judged against BASE: (a) FLIP: a `+#define NAME` line whose hunk twin is `-// #define NAME`, or a new uncommented `#define NAME` with no twin whose stem contains DEBUG, DUMP, TRACE, VERBOSE, LOG_, HEXDUMP or TIMERS (the `// #define NAME` ladder is the project's switch convention: off when the line starts with `//`). (b) UNGUARDED DUMP: an added debug_hexdump, debug_bf16dump or dump_* call outside every debug-switch `#ifdef`, in a file where a same-named call sits under one. (c) WRONG SWITCH: an added `dbg_<a>_log(` call whose text names the subject of a `dbg_<b>_log` macro the same diff adds. (d) DEBUG-ONLY INCLUDE: a header `#include` whose every use sits under one off switch. (e) TRACE PROMOTION: a TRACE_EVENT category changed from `<cat>-detail` to `<cat>`. (f) LEFTOVER: a log line starting with the author's initials, or a bare literal that gates debug text.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. BASE = merge-base of HEAD and the PR's base.sha from `gh api` (never origin/<branch> on a merged PR); to reproduce a posted comment use its original_commit_id. 2. Flips: diff the `#define` lines; keep `+#define NAME` with a `-// #define NAME` twin or no twin; drop `+//` lines and value edits. 3. Per NAME list its `#ifdef` blocks at HEAD, name what ships, count the ladder's off switches. 4. Intent: PR body, commit subjects, target branch. 5. Dumps: guard walk with a stack that counts `#ifndef`, skips comments and macro lines; GUARDED only under a ladder switch or a DEBUG-stem name. 6. Wrong switch: classify each added dbg_*_log call by its message subject. 7. Include: enumerate the included header's symbols, walk each. 8. Trace: read perfetto/apponly.cfg. 9. Leftovers: initials from `gh pr view --json author`. One question per site.
skill_entry.question: Is this switch, dump, include or trace meant to ship enabled in the target branch, and if not, which guard that the file already uses (`#ifdef GUARD`, `dbg_<subject>_log`, `<cat>-detail`) should it sit under?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: - A define that stays or arrives commented out (`// #define DEBUG_WLR` worker.cpp:86 at 247c8a4c22; `+// #define DEBUG_SAVE_KV 1` in silent PR 1722). - A value or comment edit inside an already guarded block (silent PR 2135, TOKEN_IDX_FOR_DEBUG). - A switch already on at BASE (`#define DEBUG_INFLIGHT_INIT` device.cpp:56 at worktree HEAD); the check is on the flip. - A direct spdlog::debug or spdlog::info with no adjacent dbg_*_log call, including inside another switch's block (silent PR 1827 self_attention.hpp:324 under MORE_HWATTN_DEBUG; silent PR 1973 hwattention.hpp:205-221; PR 2135 driver.cpp:294). - A dump on a path ending in std::terminate or debug_exit (2d53016b44 hwattention.hpp:503). - A dedicated debug module (src/pos/debug.cpp, PR 1707). - Anything in t/. - A trace change the PR body names as its subject. - Never block: he approves after the author answers (1973, 2011).
skill_entry.finding_shape: "`NAME` is now `#define NAME` at <file:line> (it was `// #define NAME` at BASE), so every `#ifdef NAME` block (<lines>: <logging on every dbg_x_log call / a file dump / an include>) ships; intend to leave this enabled in <branch>?" Variants: unguarded dump: "wrap in `#ifdef <GUARD>`?" (the sibling at :<line> is); wrong switch: a one-line suggestion block `dbg_<new>_log(` then "... right?", and "here too maybe?" on each further site; debug-only include: "IMO we should wrap this include in the `#ifdef <NAME>` guard"; leftover log: "still need this log?"; trace promotion: "do you really want to change this away from \"<cat>-detail\"?" with the reason from perfetto/apponly.cfg; flipped line under an "uncomment to ..." comment: "can we comment this back out before merge?"
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: A bare lowercase question, one line, no severity word: 'leaving enabled intentionally?', 'intend to leave this enabled?', 'wrap in `#ifdef WRITEBACK_HEXDUMPS`?', 'still need this log?'. The wrong-switch case is a suggestion block plus '... right?', a nit by shape. 'can we comment this back out before merge?' is the strongest form (PR 2499, target branch hwattention_sync, flipped line directly under the file's own 'uncomment to ...' comment). Never 'Nit:' or 'Coverage gap:' labels, never CHANGES_REQUESTED; he approves after the author answers, even when the switch stays on (1973, 2011; PR 3016 is still OPEN with COMMENTED reviews only).
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk (the flip or the added call); full file at HEAD (switch ladder, dbg_*_log macros, the #ifdef blocks the flip turns on, sibling guards, the depth of a printed local's declaration); BASE state of the define; other files (perfetto/apponly.cfg buffer size, fill policy and disabled_categories; h/common/perfetto.hpp category table; symbols the included header declares; includers of the header that gained the include; callers of a formatter); PR body, commit subjects and author name (initials); target branch name; comment original_commit_id when reproducing. Runtime: the Perfetto overflow rate is operator knowledge, reported as Insufficient data unless an operator statement is cited.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: a debug switch, dump, include or trace promotion that ships on

Setup: `BASE_SHA=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha); BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD $BASE_SHA)`. Never use `origin/<base branch>` for a merged PR: the merge-base is then HEAD itself and the diff is empty (2d53016b44 against origin/hwattention_sync). When reproducing a posted comment, HEAD is `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/comments/ID --jq .original_commit_id` and the line is `.original_line`; the digest's `(commit X)` is GitHub's current `commit_id`, often a later head where the author already applied the fix.

1. Flipped or new switches: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^(\+\+\+|@@)|^[-+] ?(// ?)?#define [A-Z_0-9]*(DEBUG|DUMP|TRACE|VERBOSE|LOG|HEXDUMP|TIMERS)[A-Z_0-9]*'`. Keep a line only if it starts with `+#define NAME` (no `//` before `#define`) and either (i) the same hunk has `-// #define NAME` (a flip) or (ii) no `-` line in the hunk names NAME (a new enabled switch). Discard `+// #define NAME` (a new off switch) and a `-#define NAME <old>` / `+#define NAME <new>` pair (a value edit). A flip whose stem the regex misses (13 of the 43 `// #define` lines at worktree HEAD: TRON_CALLED_ONCE, HEAP_SHADOW, PREFILL_WITH_NANS, SERIAL_DEVICE_INIT, SHOW_UNUSED_DEVICES ...) is caught by the twin rule: also run `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^-// ?#define [A-Z_0-9]+' ` and pair each with a `+#define` of the same NAME. Map to HEAD lines through the `@@` headers.
2. What the flip turns on: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n -E '#ifdef NAME|#if .*NAME|defined\(NAME\)'`; read each block and name what ships (a `dbg_*_log` macro that expands to spdlog::debug and its call count `grep -c 'dbg_x_log('`, a file dump, a fixed TOKEN_IDX_FOR_DEBUG compare, an include). Ladder context: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n -E '^(// ?)?#define [A-Z_0-9]+( [0-9]+)?$'`; a lone enabled line on a ladder of commented ones is the leftover shape. Name the other enabled switches of the ladder in the same comment (Wade named MORE_HWATTN_DEBUG from the hunk at DEBUG_GET_ALLKV).
3. Intent: `gh pr view N --json body,baseRefName -q '.baseRefName, .body' | grep -n -i -E 'debug|dump|trace|log'`; `git -C WT log --format='%h %s' --no-merges BASE..HEAD | grep -i -w -E 'enable|enabled|turn off|disable|disables|comment out|debug'`. The grep is a hint only (a misspelled subject such as 'diable it' escapes it); step 1 at the final head decides. Note the target branch. Every flip comment in the corpus (1973, 2011, 2499) is on a PR targeting the hwattention_sync feature branch; the author may answer that the switch stays on, and Wade approves. No corpus example of a flip on a main-targeted PR exists (Insufficient data for a main-specific rule).
4. Dumps and direct logs: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+.*(debug_hexdump\(|debug_bf16dump\(|[^a-z_]dump_[a-z_]*\(|spdlog::debug\()' | grep -v -E '^[0-9]+:\+ *(//|inline |void |static )'`. spdlog::info is never a trigger of this check. Hits inside a file or function the PR adds as a dump module (every function named dump_*) are a do-not-fire case; list them once as a group. Per file: ladder and macros `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n -E '#define dbg_[a-z_]*log|^// ?#define|^#ifdef'`, then the guard walk `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk '/^#if/{d++; g[d]=$0} /^#el(se|if)/{g[d]=g[d]" [else]"} /^#endif/{d--} /PATTERN/ && $0 !~ /^ *\/\// && $0 !~ /^#define/ {printf "%d: depth=%d", NR, d; for(i=1;i<=d;i++) printf " <%s>", g[i]; print ""}'` with PATTERN = `debug_hexdump\(|debug_bf16dump\(|spdlog::debug\(`. The walk counts `#ifdef`, `#ifndef` and `#if` (the old `/^#ifdef|^#if /` form missed `#ifndef NDEBUG` and gave model.hpp:1378 depth 0), prints the full guard stack only when depth > 0, marks an `#else` branch, and skips comment lines and the `#define dbg_x_log(...) spdlog::debug(__VA_ARGS__)` macro line. A hit is GUARDED only when some entry of its stack is `#ifdef NAME` or `#if defined(NAME)` with NAME on the file's ladder (`grep -n -E '^(// ?)?#define NAME' FILE` returns a line) or NAME matching the DEBUG|DUMP|TRACE|VERBOSE|LOG|HEXDUMP|TIMERS stem. A hit whose only enclosing guard is a build-configuration test (`#if TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16`, `#ifndef NDEBUG`) counts as unguarded; a hit under `#if 0` belongs to the disabled-code check, not here. Finding (dumps only: debug_hexdump, debug_bf16dump, dump_*): an unguarded added call whose same-named sibling call in the file is GUARDED (name the guard), unless the unguarded call sits on a path that reaches std::terminate() or debug_exit() within the same block. Direct spdlog::debug: never the sibling rule (the project writes spdlog::debug inside other switches' blocks, silent PR 1827); a finding only when the statement immediately before or after it (within 3 lines) calls the file's dbg_<x>_log macro and the call is at depth 0 or inside the `#ifdef` block of that macro's own switch (620d1e83ba worker.cpp:1143 under DEBUG_HWATTN_CMD_GEN, the switch of dbg_hwattn_cmds_log). Report it as a consistency nit with a suggestion block naming the macro. Mention `[[maybe_unused]]` only when a local the call prints is declared outside that guarded block: grep the local and compare its line with the block's `#ifdef`/`#endif`. A local used only inside the guarded block is the dead-symbol check's finding (2915258232), not this one.
5. Wrong switch: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+#define dbg_[a-z_]*log'`; for each file with a new macro, `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- FILE | grep -n -A1 -E '^\+.*dbg_[a-z_]*log\($'` and `... | grep -n -E '^\+.*dbg_[a-z_]*log\("'`; classify each added call by the subject its message text names (reuse, legacy wcmd, WLR); report every call on an older macro whose text names the new macro's subject, one comment per site.
6. Debug-only include: for each `+#include` in a header, enumerate the names the included header defines: `git -C WT show HEAD:INCLUDED | grep -oE '^(inline|static|constexpr|struct|class|using|void|bool|int|auto)[A-Za-z_0-9<>:, *&]* ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*) *(\(|\{|=|;)' | sed -E 's/ *(\(|\{|=|;)$//' | awk '{print $NF}' | sort -u > syms.txt`; then for each name run the step 4 walk on the includer with PATTERN = `[^A-Za-z_0-9]NAME[^A-Za-z_0-9]`. Never use a namespace as the pattern: tron::hardware is shared by several headers (on 2d53016b44 self_attention.hpp `hardware::` gives 20 depth-0 hits from other headers). If every hit is at depth >= 1 under one `#ifdef NAME` and the includer has `// #define NAME`, the include belongs under that guard. Reach of the new edge = includers of the header that gained the include (`git -C WT grep -l '<includer basename>' HEAD -- h src t bin | wc -l`) times the size of the included file (`git -C WT show HEAD:INCLUDED | wc -l`); report both numbers.
7. Trace promotion: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -B1 -A1 -E '^[-+].*TRACE_EVENT\('`; keep pairs that differ only in the category string, plus new events. Category table: `git -C WT show HEAD:h/common/perfetto.hpp | grep -n -A2 'perfetto::Category('`. Capture config: `git -C WT show HEAD:perfetto/apponly.cfg | grep -n -E 'size_kb|fill_policy|enabled_categories|disabled_categories'` (at 4d2a3951e7, 590ff29f34 and HEAD: size_kb 2097152, fill_policy DISCARD, enabled_categories "*", disabled_categories "driver-detail", "hwattention-detail", "loading"; file present since dbe388bacb, 2025-10-15). A move from a category listed under disabled_categories to one that is not adds the event to the default capture; state that from the config. Name the enclosing function and its rate (hw_prepare: once per request per layer). The overflow rate is operator knowledge: write Insufficient data unless an operator statement is cited, and ask the question instead of asserting overflow.
8. Leftovers: initials from `gh pr view N --json author -q .author.name` (mcherba -> MRC); `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+.*spdlog::(debug|info|warn)\("INITIALS '` and `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+.*\b(XXX|TEMP|HACK)\b'`. Subsystem tags (ATEM, RX, TX, FUSE, TSC, JSON, KV, HW, SW, DMA, HEAP, SLOW: 45 lines at worktree HEAD) never fire. Gating literal: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+.*\? *[a-z_]+ *: *""'`; for a hit, `git -C WT grep -n '<formatter>()' HEAD -- src h` lists the callers and whether they already select which entries print.
9. One question per site; record the author's answer; a feature-branch "stays on" answer closes the item.

On PR 1973 (BASE ec16f160f5, HEAD 5e0606f0d8): step 1 lists exactly three flips, h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp @@ -20 +20 @@ DEBUG_GET_ALLKV and @@ -25 +25 @@ MORE_HWATTN_DEBUG, src/pos/worker.cpp @@ -80 +80 @@ DEBUG_HWATTN_CMD_GEN; step 2: MORE_HWATTN_DEBUG blocks self_attention.hpp:26, :315, :353, :425, :458, :483, :783 (TOKEN_IDX_FOR_DEBUG 385 compare files), DEBUG_GET_ALLKV :21 (include pos/hwattention.hpp) and :500 (Q/K/V dump), DEBUG_HWATTN_CMD_GEN worker.cpp:117 (dbg_hwattn_cmds_log becomes spdlog::debug at its 13 call sites) and :1144; the ladder :73-:86 has 14 switches, 13 of them `// #define` and this one enabled; step 3: body has 0 debug mentions, commit 0dd3e57c66 "enable debug and shift ktok calculation", no turn-off commit, base branch hwattention_sync; step 4: four spdlog::debug adds at h/pos/hwattention.hpp:205-:221 in a file whose only switch is `// #define WRITEBACK_HEXDUMPS` and that has no dbg_*_log macro, so no finding (Wade was silent on them). Findings = 2759894229 (self_attention.hpp:20) and 2759903853 (worker.cpp:80); author answered "for the moment, yes"; APPROVED at 16:24:19Z, under three minutes after the second comment.

final.widen_delta: New check; no existing check is widened. Check 10 (hunk-to-claim) keeps its "do not fire on comment-only removed lines" rule, so a `-// #define X` / `+#define X` flip stays out of check 10 and belongs here. Check 12's placement pre-filter (`grep '#define'` on headers) lists a flipped `+#define NAME` in a header as a global definition; without its unobserved-guarantee half check 12 does not fire, and the flip is reported here only; a debug-only include edge added to a shared header belongs here (step 6). Check 13 (constant names) needs `= value` and keeps named constants; a bare output-gating literal in a condition belongs here (step 8). Overlaps with the merged taxonomy: a local that exists only inside a guarded block is dead-symbol (2915258232); spdlog::debug inside `#if 0` is disabled-code-left-in (2915191812, 3102601258); neither is reported here. Add to SKILL.md "The thirteen questions" a line 14: "Debug switch, dump, include or trace: is it meant to ship on in the target branch, and under which guard the file already uses should it sit?" and rename the list to fourteen. Add to "Words used here": switch ladder (the `// #define NAME` list at the top of worker.cpp and self_attention.hpp; a switch is off when its line starts with `//`), dbg_*_log (a per-subject logging macro that expands to spdlog::debug only when its switch is on). Add to "How Wade words a finding": one question per site, repeat sites get "here too maybe?", and a feature-branch answer that the switch stays on closes the item without a severity label. Change the common setup in procedures.md: `BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base $HEAD $(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha))` instead of `origin/main`, because a merged PR's merge-base against its own target branch is HEAD itself and a feature-branch PR's merge-base against main pulls in the whole branch.

final.precedent_note: n = 13 comments over 8 PRs (tron 1920, 1973, 2011, 2148, 2233, 2499, 2980, 3016), 2026-01-23 to 2026-06-23 (first 2719160746 on PR 1920, last 3456320516 on PR 3016). No member is pasted assistant text: none of the 13 bodies contains 'Claude' or an attribution line; all are one-line questions or suggestion blocks in Wade's own words. Six of the eight PRs target the hwattention_sync feature branch (1920, 1973, 2011, 2148, 2233, 2499); 2980 and 3016 target main; 3016 is still OPEN.
changes_made: Branch rule removed (facts lens, verified with gh pr view 2499: baseRefName hwattention_sync, state MERGED): step 3, do_not_fire and severity no longer claim a main-targeted precedent; the 'before merge' form is tied to the 'uncomment to ...' comment context and Insufficient data is stated for a main-specific rule.

BASE recipe replaced (executability lens): merge-base of HEAD and the PR's base.sha from gh api; origin/<branch> gives an empty diff on a merged PR; comment reproduction uses original_commit_id and original_line (verified: 2719160746 commit_id 2d53016b44, original_commit_id fcc9b0de95, original_line 358).

Guard walk replaced in steps 4 and 6 (all three lenses): `/^#if/` counts #ifndef, a guard stack g[d] prints only at depth > 0 (no stale label at depth 0), `#else` marked, comment lines and `#define dbg_x_log` macro lines skipped. Re-run: fcc9b0de95 hwattention.hpp :337/:361 depth 0 and :393/:425 depth 1; 2d53016b44 :409/:438/:472/:513 depth 1, :503 depth 0; 136a45018 self_attention.hpp :324/:330 depth 1 under MORE_HWATTN_DEBUG.

GUARDED definition added (executability lens): only a ladder switch or a DEBUG-stem name counts; `#if TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16` and `#ifndef NDEBUG` are depth without a guard; `#if 0` goes to the disabled-code check.

Decided between lenses on spdlog::info: removed from trigger (b) and from the step 4 regex (precision lens); no member comment concerns it and silent PR 2135 driver.cpp:294 would fire. The executability lens's regex kept spdlog::info; precision's reading is used.

Decided on the sibling rule: narrowed to dump calls (debug_hexdump, debug_bf16dump, dump_*); a direct spdlog::debug fires only through the adjacency rule, and only at depth 0 or inside the block of the dbg macro's own switch (precision fix 4 plus executability fix 8). This removes the silent-1827 false positive regardless of the awk form.

Adjacency case re-labelled a consistency nit with a suggestion block; the `[[maybe_unused]]` clause now applies only when the printed local is declared outside the guarded block (facts lens: dbg_ac1 at :1134 is inside :1128-:1147); the local-only-feeds-the-log sentence is handed to the dead-symbol check.
